From a user perspective, the component has an actionable highlighted state but does not render it. ### Expected behavior The visual highlighted/focused state should always match the option that Enter will act on. On reopen, MUI should either: restore the visible highlight on the active option, or reset the highlighted option so that Enter is a noop until an option is visibly highlighted. There should not be a state where Enter deselects an option that is not visually indicated as active. ### Context I am reporting this specifically as a visual state mismatch / keyboard UX issue, not only as “Enter deselects a selected option”. I searched for related issues before opening this one: #44936 discusses keyboard accessibility problems in the “Multiple Values” example and mentions Enter removing a selected option. #44640 discusses highlight behavior when options are already selected, but that issue was closed as expected behavior. #48093 discusses lost focus/highlight in Autocomplete after rerender. I believe this report is distinct because the core issue here is the following: after reopening the popup, an option is still actionable via Enter, but no option is visibly highlighted. title: [autocomplete] Option loses the last focus after component is rerendered
response_comment:
I found the problem. It's in the `getPreviousHighlightedOptionIndex` function 👇 
https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/b4a84d8c5ecbe2a4bf35a2eb7e2adc620393b6a7/packages/mui-material/src/useAutocomplete/useAutocomplete.js#L510-L514

This function always has a reference to the previous list of options :( 

I can try to fix it if you don't mind

Here's my attempt to fix the problem :) 

https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/48094

Hi! It won't find the highlighted item in the previous items list, because it wasn't there.

```
      const previousHighlightedOption = previousProps.filteredOptions[highlightedIndexRef.current];
```

And it won't be able to tell what to highlight if your value is controlled to `null`. For this reason I believe the example does not warrant any code change.

> Hi! It won't find the highlighted item in the previous items list, because it wasn't there.
> 
> ```
>       const previousHighlightedOption = previousProps.filteredOptions[highlightedIndexRef.current];
> ```


Yes, you're right. Autocomplete doesn't see option because it has "outdated" reference to previous filtered options. :(


> And it won't be able to tell what to highlight if your value is controlled to `null`. For this reason I believe the example does not warrant any code change.

The component still looses its focus even if I simplify my example and if I remove `value` prop. :( 
I updated example on codesandbox 👉  https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/5gc5pj

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22b740e4-f5ca-488d-b873-7163adb6c4e5


My understanding is that we have a reference to an outdated list of options because of this line:
https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/fcddb09d7f61762510c8ef78ec683b33c77d37b8/packages/mui-material/src/useAutocomplete/useAutocomplete.js#L593
We update the sync callback only when the number of options changes. 

In my proposed PR I keep reference to the previous options inside a ref, so we are sure that the reference is up to date.

> However, this rerender could be triggered by an async action at the parent component.

@VadimZvf Can you share specifics about your use-case? Your test case example makes sense, trying to understand the issue better

> [@VadimZvf](https://github.com/VadimZvf) Can you share specifics about your use-case? Your test case example makes sense, trying to understand the issue better

Hi! Sorry for the late reply 🙏

I tried to reuse the `useAutocomplete` hook inside a custom tree select component. I was checking whether it could be reused for keyboard navigation.
However, while testing it, I discovered the issue I mentioned here: `useAutocomplete` doesn’t handle a dynamic list of options well. The highlighted option breaks when options are added to or removed from its props :(
I also found that it doesn’t work well with lazy-loaded options, especially when options are injected asynchronously in the middle of the list.

In the end, I decided to use another tool for keyboard navigation, so this issue is no longer relevant for me :)
I’ll leave it up to you whether to close this issue or keep it open.
Closing for now, if anybody has a use-case that needs this please feel free to reopen or open a new issue

title: [RFC] [Autocomplete] performance improvement
body: ### What's the problem? When using `Autocomplete` with a large number of options (e.g. 10,000 items as in the [example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/#virtualization) from the docs), the component becomes noticeably laggy in `multiple` mode, even with virtualization. Here's the recording from Mac M2 Pro with CPU 4x slowdown: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/753c3aa5-1093-4c9b-99c8-0ffae3d6e404 Code sandbox - https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/mui-autocomplete-perf-qpkpsy You can see that - "Select all" is slow, but unselect all is fast - Typing in the input is slow when all options selected, but fast when no option selected So performance depends on the number of selected options. ### What are the requirements? `Autocomplete` should remain responsive and provide smooth user interaction when used with a large dataset in `multiple` mode and virtualization applied. ### What are our options? _No response_ ### Proposed solution `getOptionProps` inside `useAutocomplete` internally calls `[value].some()`. And since `getOptionProps` is called for every option we get O(n^2) when all options are selected. My proposal is to add a new prop `isOptionSelected` to let users define if an option is selected or not. I tested it, and when I use `Set.has()` instead of `Array.some()`, it significantly improves performance, so I almost don't feel any delay with my setup. Alternatively, material-ui could use `Set` internally, but it wouldn't work when `isOptionEqualToValue` is provided and doesn't use reference equality. Additionally, it makes sense to move `filterSelectedOptions` condition outside of filter function, but that's not the main problem here. ### Resources and benchmarks _No response_ **Search keywords**:

Looks related to https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/34712. What you pointed out about `getOptionProps` is particularly mentioned in https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/34712#issuecomment-2223552254.

title: [autocomplete] regression in width behavior in v7.3.8
response_comment:
Hey @kimballa thanks for opening the issue, and sorry about the outcome.

As we worked on that fix, we actually added a guard against breaking changes for users that would expect their Autocomplete to still behave as before without fullWidth passed. Essentially, passing the fullWidth prop as true to the Input if there's no fullWidth prop passed to the Autocomplete.

However, we did not guard against your use case. Since you are passing {false} and the 100% width from sx landing on the component root instead of the input, it is the expected outcome, after all. Unfortunately, it was discovered through a patch release that was not meant to break usages.

Please consider changing the usages of the component to make it take the whole space, in your example removing both fullWidth (or passing it as true to signal intention) and the sx should do. I'm sorry again for this unintentional side effect.

Thanks @silviuaavram . I appreciate the follow-up. I was able to work around things on my end. 

For what it's worth, my setup using the Autocomplete component is a _bit_ convoluted in that it's wrapped in a couple of layers of application-specific components (although many apps likely wrap MUI controls in more-complex application-specific component libraries). In any case, the `fullWidth` prop isn't actually passed in via direct prop-drilling; based on some other props, I render the component with `<Autocomplete .... fullWidth={otherProp === anotherCondition} sx={someStyleThings}>` so until this happened, I was always passing `fullWidth` explicitly one way or the other. 

I sort of understand what you're doing, but I _do_ think it's somewhat unique JSX API expectations that now `true`, `false`, and `undefined` actually have three distinct outcomes in how Autocomplete treats the prop. Boolean-typed props usually treat all false-ish values the same. If it's really not an "Autocomplete-wide" prop but is instead something you're forwarding to an internal component, that feels more like something that other MUI components put into nested `slotProps` maps that make their prop-drilled behavior explicit/visible to the caller (e.g., the `inputProps` map on the `<Select>` component).

At the very least I believe it deserves some very explicit documentation, as now it no longer behaves exactly like the `fullWidth` property used in several other components.  (Assuming your feedback implies the behavior I demonstrate is `not-a-bug`, this issue should probably turn into a documentation bug issue, as the [v7.3.8 API docs on your site](https://mui.com/material-ui/api/autocomplete/) states:

> If `true`, the input will take up the full width of its container.

... and lists the default value as `false`, which is now incorrect -- since otherwise my passing `false` in explicitly would have no effect. (It should probably list the default as `undefined` and include a note on how `undefined` and `false` are treated distinctly.)
That makes sense. I propose we update our API to make it clear that the fullWidth behaviour in Autocomplete is different, and give the reasoning for it. How's that sound, @kimballa ?

title: [popup] Popover anchorEl console.warn spam in jsdom in MUI 7.3.8
response_comment:
> I think the best way to think about testing is to set up your test env to ignore or expect certain warnings. Altering behavior of the library when a test env is detected is always going to be less robust.

I agree that altering behavior of the library based on test env is less robust, but I disagree that it shouldn't be done - rather, it becomes one of several potentially competing design criteria.

To me, it's in part a question of DX (developer experience) - I want the code I work on to "just work," to be a joy for others to use, and I appreciate it when code I use takes the same approach. I therefore appreciate libraries that go to extra effort to accommodate common usage scenarios, even if that means a bit more internal complexity. (MUI in general does really well here - robust docs with fantastic interactive examples, good types, highly customizable, transparent development process.) And there's a question of tradeoffs: an internal project, with more limited resources and with focused maintainers who can more easily learn its specifics, may choose to prioritize robustness. But MUI is very widely used - I appreciate it when it's willing to make investments to save downstream developers' time, instead of shifting costs onto a potentially large number of downstream projects.

From another perspective, altering runtime behavior based on test environment is, as you say, brittle. But this isn't really a question of runtime behavior: these `console.warn` messages only exist for developers' benefit and have no meaningful runtime effect, so we're already in the realm of DX (developer experience). Given that, choosing to invest in warnings for invalid properties but not invest in ensuring that those warnings handle common test environments feels... arbitrary? If the goal is to not vary implementation based on test vs. non-test, then I could even argue that the warning logic is a bug: there are commonly used DOM implementations (jsdom and happy-dom) for which the warnings give false positives, and MUI [generally](https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/testing/) [supports](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-rating/#testing) [using](https://mui.com/x/react-data-grid/virtualization/#disable-virtualization) these DOM implementations (as far as I can tell), so Popover should either support jsdom or (for consistency with these MUI components I linked to) at least document the limitation with workarounds.

And, on a purely practical and selfish level, this was a SemVer patch release whose only notice was a terse "\[code-infra] Remove usage of NODE_ENV=test" line in the changelog, but I now have tens of thousands of lines of log spam, across hundreds of tests, and a few dozen test failures (because they asserted on specific console.warn / console.error outputs).

Thank you for your time, and thank you for your work on MUI.

Not as elegant as the [@kimballa solution](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/47792#issuecomment-3924961278), but mocking the `getBoundingClientRect` method within the test setup file also works:

```javascript
Object.defineProperty(HTMLElement.prototype, "getBoundingClientRect", {
	configurable: true,
	value: () => ({
		width: 100,
		height: 40,
		top: 0,
		left: 0,
		bottom: 40,
		right: 100,
		x: 0,
		y: 0,
		toJSON: () => {}
	})
})
```

title: [table cell][theme] cssVariables + nativeColor: TableCell border color from palette.divider is almost white (wrong rgba)
body:
### Steps to reproduce Steps: 1. Open this link to live example: https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ujmwmxmu?file=src%2FApp.tsx 2. Confirm the label shows “**Current theme: cssVariables only**”. 3. Observe the table cell borders (especially the horizontal row dividers): they are visible (light gray). 4. Click “**SWITCH THEME**” to toggle to “**cssVariables + nativeColor**”. 5. Observe that the table borders become **much lighter / almost invisible** after switching. ### Current behavior When `cssVariables` is enabled with `nativeColor: true`, the generated border color for `TableCell` (based on `palette.divider`) becomes almost white and is barely visible. In the reproduction, the computed border color is: Actual: `rgba(250, 250, 250, 0.89)` ### Expected behavior The `TableCell` border color should be the same as (or equivalent to) the non-`nativeColor` path, which results in a clearly visible light gray border: Expected: `rgba(224, 224, 224, 1)` ### Context I am trying to use CSS variables with `nativeColor: true` to leverage native color functions and keep styling consistent. However, table borders become nearly invisible because the divider-based border color is computed incorrectly when `nativeColor` is enabled. From what I found, the root cause seems to be a mismatch in how `palette.divider` is processed: - `palette.divider` is `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12)`. - When `nativeColor` is **disabled**, MUI effectively sets the alpha to `1` first and then applies `lighten`, producing the expected border color. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/099a07da02523fe15fe88cdf00c4fc101e53f839/packages/mui-system/src/colorManipulator/colorManipulator.js#L245-L259 - When `nativeColor` is **enabled**, MUI uses `color-mix()` to mix the divider color with `transparent` at `0%`. This **does not** change the color at all, so the alpha remains `0.12`, and then `lighten` is applied. The result becomes nearly white and incorrect for borders. https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/099a07da02523fe15fe88cdf00c4fc101e53f839/packages/mui-material/src/styles/createThemeWithVars.js#L224-L239 This makes table borders hard to see and hurts accessibility/visual clarity. ### Your environment
npx @mui/envinfo ``` System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200 Binaries: Node: 24.13.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE npm: 11.6.2 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD pnpm: 8.5.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\pnpm.CMD Browsers: Chrome: 144.0.7559.133 Edge: Chromium (141.0.3537.71) npmPackages: @emotion/react: ^11.14.0 => 11.14.0 @emotion/styled: ^11.14.1 => 11.14.1 @mui/icons-material: ^7.3.7 => 7.3.7 @mui/material: ^7.3.7 => 7.3.7 @mui/x-data-grid: ^8.27.0 => 8.27.0 @types/react: ^19.2.13 => 19.2.13 react: ^19.2.4 => 19.2.4 react-dom: ^19.2.4 => 19.2.4 typescript: ^5.9.3 => 5.9.3 ```

title: [theme] Material UI CSS Variables not respected for derived component colors when using external stylesheet
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Open the provided StackBlitz link and inspect the Alert component's background color: https://stackblitz.com/edit/nze14hel?file=src%2FDemo.tsx

### Current behavior

Many MUI components generate derived colors (like Alert backgrounds, Slider tracks, Switch disabled states) using **JavaScript color manipulation at theme initialization time**, which bakes in the **default palette values** instead of referencing the CSS variables.

**Example with Alert component:**

When using a standard Alert with `color="info"`, the background color uses the default MUI blue (lightened by 90%) instead of our `--mui-palette-info-*` CSS variable defined in our stylesheet.

The generated CSS variable looks like:
```
--mui-palette-Alert-infoStandardBg: rgb(229, 246, 253); // 👈 Hardcoded color value based on default palette
```

This means CSS variables are **completely ignored**.

### Expected behavior

Derived component colors should reference the CSS variables so they update dynamically when the base palette variables are overridden in external stylesheets.

**Possible Solution**

Generate the CSS variable by using the color-mix function and referencing the CSS variables:

```css
--mui-palette-Alert-infoStandardBg: color-mix(in srgb, var(--mui-palette-info-light), #fff 90%);
```

### Context

We have a micro frontend architecture where multiple apps need to share a consistent theme. To maintain this centrally, we've created a single CSS file containing MUI CSS variables (e.g., --mui-palette-info-light, --mui-palette-info-main, etc.) that gets loaded by all micro frontends.

Our `createTheme` configuration is minimal and only enables CSS variables support:

```javascript
const theme = createTheme({
  cssVariables: true,
});
```

The actual color values are defined in our external CSS file:

```css
:root {
  --mui-palette-info-light: #dfc21f;
  --mui-palette-info-main: #d3b613;
  --mui-palette-info-dark: #b89f11;
  /* ... etc */
}
```

This approach is similar to the pattern described in the MUI documentation for aliasing color variables.

**Expected benefit**: We can update colors centrally in the CSS file and all micro frontends immediately reflect the changes without rebuilding or redeploying individual applications.

### Your environment

Order ID: 115541

**Search keywords**: Theme, CSS Variables, palette
response_comment: @sodehl Would you like to close the issue?

@ZeeshanTamboli Just to clarify: does this mean that all MUI CSS variables defined through an external CSS file must be referenced in the theme options in order for the generated CSS variables to build upon them?
For example: if we introduce a new CSS variable `--mui-palette-common-onBackground` in our external stylesheet, would all frontends that consume this stylesheet need to reference this variable in their `createTheme` options to ensure that any subsequently generated CSS variables are based on it?

> @ZeeshanTamboli Just to clarify: does this mean that all MUI CSS variables defined through an external CSS file must be referenced in the theme options in order for the generated CSS variables to build upon them? For example: if we introduce a new CSS variable `--mui-palette-common-onBackground` in our external stylesheet, would all frontends that consume this stylesheet need to reference this variable in their `createTheme` options to ensure that any subsequently generated CSS variables are based on it?

Yes. Any custom CSS variables you define need to be referenced in the theme options. At the moment, you also need to reference the CSS variables generated by Material UI. Once the [proposal shown above](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/issues/47740#issuecomment-3882912337) is implemented, referencing Material UI-generated CSS variables should no longer be necessary.
@ZeeshanTamboli thanks for clarifying. Should I keep this issue open to track the proposal mentioned by @siriwatknp?

@ZeeshanTamboli I noticed another issue with the current approach:

When referencing MUI CSS variables in `createTheme` as described above, I get console warnings for certain values like palette.divider:

```
Demo.tsx:7 MUI: Can't create `palette.dividerChannel` because `palette.divider` is not one of these formats: #nnn, #nnnnnn, rgb(), rgba(), hsl(), hsla(), color().
To suppress this warning, you need to explicitly provide the `palette.dividerChannel` as a string (in rgb format, for example "12 12 12") or undefined if you want to remove the channel token.

Demo: https://stackblitz.com/edit/nze14hel-zah7msat?file=src%2FDemo.tsx,src%2Findex.css

It seems the values can't be parsed correctly when referencing CSS variables like `--mui-palette-divider`, preventing channel variables from being generated. Would this also be resolved by @siriwatknp's proposal?

> Should I keep this issue open to track the proposal mentioned by @siriwatknp?

Yes.  I'll create a PR soon.

> [@ZeeshanTamboli](https://github.com/ZeeshanTamboli) I noticed another issue with the current approach:
> 
> When referencing MUI CSS variables in `createTheme` as described above, I get console warnings for certain values like palette.divider:
>

> Demo.tsx:7 MUI: Can't create `palette.dividerChannel` because `palette.divider` is not one of these formats: #nnn, #nnnnnn, rgb(), rgba(), hsl(), hsla(), color().
> To suppress this warning, you need to explicitly provide the `palette.dividerChannel` as a string (in rgb format, for example "12 12 12") or undefined if you want to remove the channel token.
> ```

> 
> It seems the values can't be parsed correctly when referencing CSS variables like `--mui-palette-divider`, preventing channel variables from being generated. Would this also be resolved by [@siriwatknp](https://github.com/siriwatknp)'s proposal?

It's a different bug. It is not parsing CSS variable (`var(--mui-palette-divider)`). Actually this should not be run when `nativeColor` is used. title: Feature Request: onBlur should behave like onChange and receive the same parameters in Autocomplete
body:
### The problem in depth

Component: Autocomplete
Use case: multiple + freeSolo

Problem Statement

In MUI Autocomplete, there is an inconsistency between onChange and onBlur:

- onBlur does not provide the same parameters as onChange (reason, details, validated value)
- onChange is only triggered after MUI validation succeeds
- onBlur fires even when the input value is invalid

This makes it impossible to handle onBlur using the same logic as onChange.

Code Example & Explanation

In our implementation, we rely on onChange for validation and value acceptance. When a value is invalid, we simply return early and the value is not added, which works as expected.
```

const handleUnitIdChange = (_, newValue, reason, details) => {
  const changedUnitId = details?.option?.trim();

  // Validation
  if (!isValid(changedUnitId)) {
    return; // value is NOT added
  }
  setUnitIds(newValue);
};
```

With `onChange`, this logic works correctly because:

- The handler is only called after MUI validation succeeds
- `reason `and `details `are available
- Returning early prevents invalid values from being committed

However, when trying to apply the same logic on onBlur, it is not possible:

```
<Autocomplete
  multiple
  freeSolo
  onChange={handleUnitIdChange}
  onBlur={() => {
    // No access to:
    // - newValue
    // - reason
    // - details
    // - validated input
  }}
/>
```


Because onBlur:

- Does not provide newValue, reason, or details
- Fires even when the input value is invalid
- Does not respect the same internal validation rules

As a result:

- Even if we return early in onBlur, the value may already be added
- We cannot reuse the same validation logic used in onChange
- Developers are forced to manually track inputValue and replicate MUI’s internal logic

Requested Improvement (Summary)

To allow consistent handling, onBlur should either:

- Receive the same parameters as onChange
- or
- Trigger onChange internally when a value is valid on blur
- or
- Respect the same validation rules and prevent invalid commits

This would allow developers to reuse the same logic and avoid unintended value additions.

```

```

> could you please help me to understand if its possible to change the default size of OutlinedInput to "small" and still be able to use "medium" size on the TextField?

@liorbd22 Yes, you can. You can explicitly set the Input's slot size for TextField:

title: [docs] Add necessary imports to Typescript theme augmentation example
response_comment:
Hi! I’ve created a PR for this issue:
https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/47426

Please let me know if any changes are needed.
This is my first contribution to MUI — thank you!
It depends if you are in the declaration file (`.d.ts`) file or a TS file (`.ts`, `.tsx` file). Only if you are in the declaration file, you need the import. So, it is about TS knowledge.

@ZeeshanTamboli Thank you, I was unaware of this. Given TypeScript's popularity and the number of people making this mistake, I still think the docs would benefit from some mention of this to avoid future issues about this topic. Perhaps specifying the file type as .d.ts (or .ts) or linking to the TypeScript docs?

Thanks for the suggestion. In practice this isn't something we can realistically document every time we show a TypeScript module-augmentation example. Whether an import is needed depends entirely on where the code lives (a `.d.ts` file vs a regular `.ts/.tsx` file), and that's standard TypeScript behaviour rather than something specific to Material UI.

If we start calling this out in one place, we'd have to do it consistently everywhere module augmentation appears across the docs, which adds a lot of noise and maintenance cost. Our goal is to keep the examples focused on what's specific to Material UI, and rely on the TypeScript documentation for the general language rules.

That said, we understand how this can trip people up and we appreciate you raising it. We'll keep an eye on whether there's a clearer, higher-level place in the docs to mention common TS patterns without cluttering each example. I think we can close this issue.

title: [FocusTrap] Inputs in shadow dom not selectable (since 7.3.6)
body:
## Steps to reproduce Steps: 1. Open this link to live example: https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/elegant-keller-pxswkw 2. Click on "open modal" 3. Attempt to change the value of the input field in the modal ### Current behavior The input field is not really selectable and the input value can not be changed. It seems as if the focus is lost right after it is selected. ### Expected behavior The input field should be selectable, even if it was rendered within a shadow dom. ## Context ### Where does this become an issue? Some UI libraries have the (exceptionally bad) concept to adjust styling and behavior after the intial DOM has loaded using a script to replace stuff with shadow roots. In our case, this is a corporate library that we must use to display e.g. input fields. We're using MUI as that library is not providing layouts/patterns/components for everything, and the remaining stuff is implemented with MUI. This automatically introduces some mix of components, e.g. we want a Popup that has a text box. The library has text fields (`input`) but it does not provide a way to create a popup. In the [codesandbox mentioned above](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/compassionate-wave-pxswkw), this is "simulated" - we use `` for the Popup implementation, and a `` for the text field. Like with the library, the `` is placed in a shadow DOM. With that setup, changing the text of the input is not possible anymore. ### Culprit: v7.3.6 I **believe** that I've pinpointed the issue down to these two commits: https://github.com/mui/material-ui/commit/5536c153f5007b3756979cb19cd3ac6fc3febb7a https://github.com/mui/material-ui/commit/15ff3955e950f3d1ee70b0ea9d9fd8c1057ee0cb Specifically, the `FocusTrap` seems to be interfering here. I strongly believe that the `FocusTrap` should not interfere with non-MUI elements in a way, that renders them dysfunctional. Using the same code, but with v7.3.5, the code from the codesandbox works. If you try it out, make sure to delete 'node_modules', as the `^7.3.5` notation for the mui/utils package would allow npm to keep the 'faulty' implementation. ## Your environment
npx @mui/envinfo ``` Issue exists (at least) in chrome and firefox System: OS: Linux 6.1 Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye) 11 (bullseye) Binaries: Node: 20.19.5 - /usr/local/bin/node npm: 10.8.2 - /usr/local/bin/npm pnpm: Not Found Browsers: Chrome: Not Found Firefox: Not Found npmPackages: @emotion/react: 11.14.0 @emotion/styled: ^11.14.1 => 11.14.1 @mui/core-downloads-tracker: 7.3.6 @mui/material: 7.3.6 => 7.3.6 @mui/material-nextjs: 7.3.6 => 7.3.6 @mui/private-theming: 7.3.6 @mui/styled-engine: 7.3.6 @mui/system: 7.3.6 @mui/types: 7.4.9 @mui/utils: 7.3.6 @types/react: 18.2.25 => 18.2.25 react: 18.2.0 => 18.2.0 react-dom: 18.2.0 => 18.2.0 typescript: 5.2.2 => 5.2.2 ```
**Search keywords**: input shadow dom selectable
response_comment:
Thanks for the reproduction.

This issue occurs because the `input` element lives inside a Shadow DOM that is _not_ part of the Modal's DOM subtree. Since v7.3.6, the FocusTrap became Shadow-DOM aware via `getActiveElement`, but the containment check it uses (`root.contains(...)`) is still Shadow-DOM unaware. As a result, the trap thinks focus has escaped and immediately pulls it back.

You can work around this by adding:

```jsx
<Dialog disableEnforceFocus ...>
```

(or on `Modal` / `Popover`, depending on the component you use). See https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/mui-7-3-6-input-shadow-root-issue-forked-x6nm3c

This prevents `FocusTrap` from forcibly re-capturing focus and allows the Shadow-DOM input to behave normally.

---

Before 7.3.6:

- `activeElement` was just `doc.activeElement`, usually the host (`#host`) or some element the trap considered "inside".

- `rootElement.contains(doc.activeElement)` returned `true`.

So `FocusTrap` did not try to steal focus back and everything appeared to “work” (by accident).

---

Maybe the solution is to update the `FocusTrap` logic so that the "is focus inside the trap?" check becomes Shadow-DOM aware as well i.e, climbing through the composed tree instead of relying on `Node.contains()`. This would allow Shadow-DOM-hosted inputs to work without disabling focus enforcement.

title: Switch physical direction props to logical ones (inline-start / inline-end) for better bidi support
body:
### Summary

I’d like to propose updating MUI’s component internals so that CSS logical properties are used (`inline-start`, `inline-end`, `margin-inline-start`, etc.) instead of physical `left`/`right`/`margin-left`/`margin-right`.

**Rationale**

Even with `theme.direction = 'rtl'`, several MUI components still require manual prop changes because their internal styles rely on physical properties or DOM order rather than logical properties. Examples include:

* `Button` icon placement (`startIcon` / `endIcon`)
* `Chip` delete/action icon positioning
* `FormControlLabel` margins
* Various components using `marginLeft`/`marginRight` instead of logical equivalents

As a result, bidi apps must manually swap props or override internal styles even when the theme direction is set correctly. Using logical properties internally would ensure that components automatically follow the writing mode without additional work from the developer.

**Proposal**

* Replace internal physical layout properties with logical CSS properties.
* Avoid introducing new optional layers or alternative props; the goal is to align the underlying implementation with logical-direction standards so that components behave correctly in both LTR and RTL out of the box.

This change should not affect user-facing APIs, only internal styling, so backwards compatibility can be maintained while significantly improving RTL/bidi correctness.

I’m willing to implement this and submit a PR, but I’d like confirmation from the maintainers that switching the internal styling model to logical properties is acceptable before starting.

Please advise on whether this direction would be approved or whether it has been discussed previously.

### Examples

_No response_

### Motivation

I developed many projects using MUI, all of them in at least two languages, one LTR and one RTL. The RTL theme needed a lot of extra configurations just to get margins and positioning right, as simply changing the theme direction to "rtl" didn't change everything.

**Search keywords**: bidi, inline, rtl, left, right, logical directions

title: [docs] Weak CSP nonce guidance
body:
### Related page

https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/content-security-policy/

### Kind of issue

Other

### Issue description

The current documentation says:

> A CSP nonce is a Base 64 encoded string. You can generate one like this:
```js
import uuidv4 from 'uuid/v4';

const nonce = new Buffer(uuidv4()).toString('base64');
```
> You must use UUID version 4, as it generates an unpredictable string.

This generates a random string with 122 bits of entropy, which is less than the 128 bits prescribed by the [Content Security Policy Level 3
W3C Working Draft](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#security-nonces):

> The generated value SHOULD be at least 128 bits long (before encoding), and SHOULD be generated via a cryptographically secure random number generator in order to ensure that the value is difficult for an attacker to predict.

Better implementation guidance might be:

```js
import crypto from 'crypto';

const nonce = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64'); // 128 bits of entropy
```

It's also worth noting that `new Buffer(array)` is [deprecated](https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#new-bufferarray) as of Node 6.0.0.

Instead of applying padding directly to input, apply padding to wrapper - this fixes the caret positioning | ## Proposed Solution Move the padding from the input element to the wrapper/root container. This ensures: - ✅ The input fills the entire clickable area (no padding gaps) - ✅ All clicks in the padded area hit the input directly - ✅ The browser's native caret positioning works correctly **Verified:** I've tested this fix by removing padding from the input element in browser DevTools, and the caret positioning works as expected. ### Steps to reproduce Steps: 1. Open this link to live example: https://stackblitz.com/run?file=src%2FDemo.tsx 2. Inspect the `

title: [tooltip] `aria-label` overwrites trigger's visible text
body: ### Steps to reproduce Steps: 1. Open this link to live example: https://mui.com/material-ui/react-tooltip/ 2. Look at the tooltip code (the HTML generated in the browser console) 3. There is an aria-label attribute inside the button 4. That will unfortunately overwrite the button content, for assistive technologies like screen readers. ### Current behavior The aria-label inside the button is erasing the accessible name of this button, like: `` Screen readers will here read "Button add", instead of "Button Margin add". ### Expected behavior The aria-label inside the button should be removed, like: `` To provide an accessible tooltip, we should only generate a text in the span inside this button, when focusing it. ### Context Make the MUI tooltip more accessible (comprehensive) for screen reader users. ### Your environment Chrome v142, tested with NVDA. **Search keywords**: tooltip
response_comment: Ok, your workaround (unset the aria-label) seems good, many thanks!

I noticed we take a label default approach for the tooltip, and also provide a description optional approach, in the [Accessibility](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-tooltip/#accessibility) section. I believe our docs content is correct, but I would like to propose some improvements. [FluentUI Tooltip](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs#relationship-label) is in a similar situation and chooses to address the relationship concept in the docs as one of the first sections. I believe we should do the same.

- Keep the Accessibility section but change its content, the way [Fluent](https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/?path=/docs/components-tooltip--docs#accessibility) and [React Spectrum](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/v3/Tooltip.html#accessibility) do, and focus on the interactivity of the trigger details, and possibly other accessibility concerns.
- Create a new section right below [Basic tooltip](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-tooltip/#basic-tooltip) named Relationship or something similar, where we describe the default label behavior and optional via prop description behavior. It should be more or less our current Accessibility content, with the describeChild prop.
- Change the examples with visible text as triggers to have only describeChild prop tooltips, since that's the behavior we want to show anyway: buttons that already have visible text label, but with a tooltip that complements that information.

I believe these changes will improve the relationship information about the tooltip and its trigger, how MUI works under the hood, and will remove the ambiguity that could happen like in the above GH issue. I would love to hear your opinion! I can also create an GH issue with this content, for tracking, or use the already created GH issue so we don't duplicate.

It's great to see that the examples have been improved, but isn't this an issue that still needs to be fixed in the component? The Tooltip continues to override the trigger's accName by default.

I don't know if there is a meta-issue for MUI v8 (or if it will even happen), but this change would be a great candidate for the next major release, because Tooltip is such a commonly used component.
@mayank99 what do you mean by fixing it? The behaviors are working as expected. Could you provide an example?

@silviuaavram The issue is like I said above: "The Tooltip continues to override the trigger's accName by default", which is very unexpected.

The following example looks perfectly normal and will easily pass code review, but the `title` overrides the button's visible label, creating an instant [WCAG SC 2.5.3](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html) violation.

```jsx
<Tooltip title="here's how you use the thing">
  <Button>the thing</Button>
</Tooltip>
```

The simplest way of "fixing it" would be by changing the default value of `describeChild` to `true`. The default value is important because most developers who use MUI are not even aware of the `describeChild` prop — a point which is proved by the fact that MUI's own examples weren't using this prop until recently.

Ideally, the default value of `describeChild` would depend on whether the trigger already has a label. But that might be tricky to implement correctly.

@mayank99 I don't think we will change the behavior, for a number of reasons:
1. it's been around for some time now, it's a big breaking change and I don't believe it's worth switching one default for another.
2. as far as moving forward, the desired behavior is actually the one in [BaseUI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tooltip), which is even more breaking, but it makes sense for the tooltip to only label the trigger visually, while the consumer will label the trigger for assisted tech as well. What material-ui does right now is giving you both (visual + aria label) via Trigger `title` prop.
3. the describe child is not a default because, if there's any additional information that needs to be conveyed about a control, it should always be visible, like adding description below textfields/textareas instead of putting it in a tooltip, which is not going to be visible on mobile, and you'll be missing that information.

There are quite a few libraries out there that have the aria-describedby behavior by default, that's true. But, ideally, given the mobile constraint (tooltips are not shown on mobile), we believe that Tooltips should only be used for visual enhancement, for instance icon buttons whose behaviors are not straightforward.

For these reasons we will keep Tooltip's behavior as it is right now, and not deliver any breaking change. The docs should now help consumers better understand better if a tooltip should be used, and how.

title: [autocomplete] Inconsistent behavior between single and multiple rendered values
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Steps:
1. Open this link to live example: [Single Value Rendering](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/#single-value-rendering)
2. Compare behavior for the following between single value and [multiple value rendering](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/#multiple-values).
3. Generally multiple value rendering behaves as I'd expect except where noted below.

## ArrowLeft

### Single value

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. Press left and observe that the set value is selected.

With no input present the set value is selected.

### Multiple value

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. Press left and observe that no set value is selected.
4. No matter where the cursor is no value is every selected when pressing ArrowLeft.

With no input present the most recent picked value is selected.

For either multiple or single I would think that a value could be selected if the cursor is at the beginning of the input, but at least it should have consistent behavior between the two.

## Delete

### Single value

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. Press delete and observe that the set value is deleted and that the deletion is sent to the input field as well deleting input text depending on where the cursor is.

### Multiple values

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. Press delete and observe that no set value is removed and that only text is removed. To delete a set value it must first be selected. This is regardless of whether input is present or not.

## Backspace

### Single value

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. Press backspace and the set value is removed and the backspace is sent to the input field as well.

### Multiple value

1. Set a value and type some input.
2. Place your cursor anywhere in the input field.
3. No value is removed and backspace only ever affects text input unless all input is removed. If a value is selected and backspace is pressed it will remove that selected value.

title: [autocomplete] Keeping the filter value after selecting an option
body:
### Summary

The Autocomplete component like in the ['Checkboxes' example](https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/#checkboxes) should offer the possibility to select multiple options while the input (i.e. filter) is kept. The current implementation deletes the input after an option was selected. The behaviour is different when deselecting an option.

### Examples

Let's assume the user wants to select all movie titles (like in the 'Checkboxes' example) that start with "The". Currently, the input is reset after selecting an option, even if clearOnBlur is set to false. This means the user has to enter the filter value again, before the next option can be selected.
Interestingly, the proposed behaviour is already there when an option is deselected (and clearOnBlur is set to false). The input values is kept while the option is removed. 

### Motivation

I would like to speed up the seletion of multiple similar options.

If there is a good reason for the differences between select and deselect, I would like to know.

**Search keywords**: Autocomplete multiple clearOnBlur checkboxes

[Collapse] Add slotProps Support to Collapse for Customizing Inner Elements
body:
### Summary

The Collapse] component in Material UI currently does not support passing custom props or styles to its inner wrapper elements (MuiCollapse-wrapper, MuiCollapse-wrapperInner). This limitation makes it difficult to apply ARIA roles, custom classes, or styles for accessibility and design consistency.

I propose adding a slotProps API to Collapse, similar to other Material UI components, allowing developers to pass props directly to these internal elements.

### Examples

Many other MUI components (e.g., Popover, Menu, Dialog) support slotProps for customizing internal structure.

```tsx
<Collapse in={open} timeout="auto" slotProps=
    {{
        root: 
        {
            // Custom ARIA role for accessibility
            role: "presentation",
            // Custom class for styling
            className: "custom-collapse-root",
            // Custom data attribute
            "data-testid": "collapse-root",
        },
        wrapper: 
        {
            role: "presentation",
            className: "custom-collapse-wrapper",
            sx: { marginLeft: 2  /* Example custom style */ },
        },
        wrapperInner: 
        {
            role: "group",
            className: "custom-collapse-wrapper-inner",
            component: "ul", // Change the component type
            sx: { listStyle: "none", padding: 0, margin: 0  /* Example custom style */ },
        },
    }}>
    <Box component="li" role="treeitem" sx={{ p: 2 }}>
        Child Item 1
    </Box>
    <Box component="li" role="treeitem" sx={{ p: 2 }}>
        Child Item 2
    </Box>
</Collapse>
```

### Motivation

In complex applications, especially those requiring strict accessibility compliance (e.g., ARIA roles for tree views), developers need fine-grained control over the DOM structure.

Currently, the inability to add props to Collapse's inner elements leads to invalid HTML (e.g., `<ul>` → `<div>` → `<div>` → `<li>`) and prevents adding `role="presentation"` or custom classes for styling and accessibility.
Introducing slotProps would align Collapse with other MUI components, improve accessibility, and enable more flexible customization for real-world use cases.

**If this is implemented, it will also benefit the MUI X TreeView component, which uses Collapse internally. This could enable improved accessibility setups in MUI X and related components.**

**Search keywords**: Collapse, slotProps, customization, accessibility, props, slot
response_comment:
@NotYoojun It looks to me that those inner `Wrapper`s are an implementation detail of the design and not intended to be customizable slots

If it's a viable option for you, the Collapsible component from our headless library doesn't have these issues and is much more customizable: https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible
Actually, we could add the `slots` and `slotProps` to make it consistent with the rest of the components. cc @sai6855 if you have time, feel free to grab this one.

title: [customization] Added props are directly passed to DOM element
body:
### Steps to reproduce

In our own theme we augment an extra prop to Button, called `dense`. But the issue is on all elements where we add an extra prop.

```ts
declare module '@mui/material/Button' {
  interface ButtonOwnProps {
    dense?: boolean
  }
```

Now that totally works, we can use the prop in our styleOverride when creating our theme (using `createTheme`). But in the end it also lands in its DOM. Because in MUI components only MUI specifics per component are guarded to not end up there. In our example for Button MUI prevents:

https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/packages/mui-material/src/Button/Button.js#L78-L82
```ts
const ButtonRoot = styled(ButtonBase, {
  shouldForwardProp: (prop) => rootShouldForwardProp(prop) || prop === 'classes',
```

https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/master/packages/mui-material/src/styles/slotShouldForwardProp.ts#L2-L4
```ts
function slotShouldForwardProp(prop: string) {
  return prop !== 'ownerState' && prop !== 'theme' && prop !== 'sx' && prop !== 'as';
}
```

### Current behavior

It passes newly added props directly to the DOM. Because MUI leans on Emotion. And Emotion doesn't like the [transcient prop](https://github.com/emotion-js/emotion/issues/2193) setup Styled Components is using, where we can use `$` to filter these out.

### Expected behavior

Maybe MUI can support the concept of a transcient prop, or at least tell which prop to not forward. Since externally we do not want a prop to be named `$dense` but `dense` :)

### Context

We want to be as close as possible to MUI. We create its theme and use all existing props and additions. Which makes MUI very flexible. But the price we pay is that attributes get all the way to its DOM node itself. For which we should get a solution. Is ownerState the only solution?

### Your environment

in all versions of MUI same behaviour


**Search keywords**: shouldforward, emotion
response_comment: @maapteh In your app are you making custom UI components that wrap Material UI components (and add extra props etc), or importing directly from `@mui/material` throughout?

> We tried not to forward it on our own styled composition, but then of course it doesn't land on the ownProps of MUI as well 

So you mean even the config shown below doesn't work for you in your custom styled component?
```
shouldForwardProp: (prop) => prop !== "dense"
```

If the issue persists, please share a minimal reproduction on StackBlitz, CodeSandbox, or a small GitHub repo. Also check existing issues to see if a similar one already exists.

body: ### Steps to reproduce 1. **Device:** iPhone 14 Pro Max, **OS:** iOS 26.0 2. **Browser:** Safari or Chrome on iOS (both are WebKit-based) 3. Reproduces in both Safari and Chrome on iOS 26.0. ### Expected behavior The `Drawer` and its `Backdrop` should cover the entire viewport, including the bottom safe area, with no visible gap, regardless of the browser toolbar state. ### Context This appears to be an interaction between iOS 26 viewport/safe-area changes and how `Modal`/`Backdrop` are positioned (fixed with `inset: 0`). On iOS, without `viewport-fit=cover`, the layout viewport can end above the bottom safe area, so the Backdrop stops short. ### Your environment - **Material UI:** latest on docs; also reproduced in my app - **iOS:** 26.0 (iPhone 14 Pro Max) - **Browsers:** Safari (iOS), Chrome (iOS) ### Search keywords iOS 26, Safari, Chrome iOS, Material UI Drawer, Modal Backdrop, safe area, viewport-fit=cover, inset: 0, 100dvh
response_comment:
https://nitter.net/devongovett/status/1968384768703349198#m

This is probably worth a try:

> Safari clips fixed elements to the "inner" viewport (even with negative position), which means the backdrop will not extend behind the status bar or address bar.
>
> 1. Use position: absolute instead of position: fixed for the backdrop. This will position relative to the entire page rather than the viewport.
> 2. Set the backdrop height to match the entire height of the page (or set position: relative on the body) so it is guaranteed to cover the viewport no matter the scroll position.
> 3. Add an extra position: sticky div around the modal itself so that it appears in view instead of at the top of the page when scrolled down.
Corresponding issue in Base UI: https://github.com/mui/base-ui/issues/2799

<Stepper

title: v4.x: Orphaned stylesheets due to skipped effect in useSynchronousEffect
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Demo: https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/mui4-make-styles-repro-c7h95p?file=%2Fsrc%2FList.js%3A19%2C22

Steps:
1. Switch the list on by clicking TOGGLE LIST.
2. Observe that stylesheet LIST appears.
3. Switch the list off by clicking TOGGLE LIST button again.
4. Observe that stylesheet LIST is not removed.

### Current behavior

LIST stylesheet remains in the DOM after the component is unmounted, leading to potential memory leaks and stale styles.

### Expected behavior

LIST stylesheet should be properly detached and cleaned up even when React skips effects due to state updates during render.

### Context

In our legacy project, we dynamically mount one of several applications on the page at any given time. Each application is delivered as a separate bundle and includes its own instance of Material-UI. We commonly use state updates during render to optimize our workflow. As a result, we’ve encountered some similar issues where stylesheets from a previously mounted application are not properly cleaned up, leading to conflicts with the styles of the currently mounted application.

We investigated a bit this issue and found out that it occurs because `useSynchronousEffect` stores its cleanup function in a local variable, which is lost if React skips the effect.

Also we fixed the issue by using a ref for the cleanup function, so it persists across renders and ensure proper cleanup.

For now we have patched makeStyles module locally. I'm going to create PR later.

### Your environment

Browser: Chrome (latest)
Material UI version: 4.11.3
React: ^17

**Search keywords**: useSynchronousEffect, orphaned stylesheets, effect skipping, React, makeStyles, cleanup bug

**Search keywords**: autocomplete, multiple, free solo
response_comment: `options` array is empty. Why are you not providing any options? Works well with options: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-n8vef1u1-i3znh9a9.
@ZeeshanTamboli Because I want to use the component as a field for multiple new elements

Okay, it's because you are using `autoHighlight` with freeSolo + multiple. If there are no options to highlight, why are you using `autoHighlight`?

What’s happening under the hood

- With multiple + freeSolo, pressing Enter should add the current input as a new chip, even if it doesn’t exist in options.
- When autoHighlight is on, the hook tries to pre-select “the first filtered option.”
- If options is empty (or filtering yields none), that highlight step still runs and ends up reading properties of an undefined option (e.g., calling label/equality logic on undefined) during the same Enter flow — causing the crash.

title: Scrolling on AutoComplete and pressing Enter causes item to be selected
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Steps:
1. Go to the official docs: https://mui.com/material-ui/react-autocomplete/#combo-box
2. In mobile mode, enter a search term, e.g. "e" and then scroll by dragging an item vertically
3. Press enter on the keyboard

### Current behavior

The item which was placed under the initial touch point of the scrolling is selected.

### Expected behavior

No item is selected (the same behaviour as when no scrolling was done).

### Context

_No response_

### Your environment

_No response_

**Search keywords**: combo-box,scrolling,autocomplete
response_comment: I can reproduce this with a real device, could be considered a bug

Hi maintainers 👋
I’d like to work on this issue.
Please let me know if it’s already assigned to someone.
Thanks!

`setHighlightedIndex` on option touchstart is needed here to set the focused state (and class) so you can see which option is being touched

According to claude code, removing highlight on touchEnd would cause these issues:

> - It would remove the highlight even for valid taps (touch → release → click). Since handleOptionClick runs after touchEnd, the highlight would flicker away before the click visually confirms the selection.
> - It doesn’t distinguish between a tap (should keep highlight) and a scroll (should clear it). You’d need to check scroll state in the touchEnd handler anyway, which is essentially what we’re doing with touchScrolledRef.

@silviuaavram I included this issue with 2 other fixes in the same PR as they all essentially require tracking the highlight reason (kb, mouse or touch) internally to differentiate between these cases
